what: Deliverable 3 of the balance baseline (2026-11-21): the target specification. Every target names its class, metric, band, scope, reader, source and date. The words are docs/design/balance-baseline/03-targets.md. The check is node tools/balance-program/targets.mjs --check
base: set/v0.2.144 at 861ae52e3 (branch baseline/overhaul-start), the overhaul's starting build and not the live game. Readers are standards.mjs as it stands there
status: INVENTORY (re-scope 2026-11-21): the overhaul design is reset from first principles and the book is a candidate design with no authority. Balance targets come after the new design is defined. Every target here is a candidate, labelled DESIGN HYPOTHESIS. Only the constraints are hard

classes.HARD: Used only in constraints: the mission lines of CLAUDE.md section 1 and genuine technical limits
classes.SOFT: Not used in the inventory. Kept for the target work that follows
classes.HYPOTHESIS: Every inventoried target. A candidate from an old ruling, the overhaul book, a designer ruling or a measurement

forms.rule: its source asked a never, an always or an ordering
forms.proposal: its source proposed a number nobody ruled

sourceKinds.old-ruling: a dated ruling of Tyler's, sittings and page picks included
sourceKinds.overhaul-book: the overhaul book or the 50-standards auditor (PROVISIONAL or PROPOSED)
sourceKinds.designer-ruling: a designer ruling, D-1 to D-11
sourceKinds.measurement: a reading of the real engine

constraints.rule: Multiplayer-only, online-only and server-authoritative. Every outcome a target reads is computed by the server engine on server state. The client never authors a number, and no solo or client-side tier exists
Hunts keep running on the server after the browser closes, until stamina, supplies, gold, death or another end reason stops them. A target reads the same with the hunt viewed or the browser closed
One combat engine runs every hunt, viewed or not: 10 s settlement and 100 ms combat steps, with no second path. Every reading comes from that engine, never a second balance engine
constraints.source: CLAUDE.md section 6. The baseline directive, phase 7

constraints.rule: A cell of 128 hero-hours cannot see a death rate under about 23 in 1,000 hours. Rare-event targets are read on pooled samples of at least 4 seeds of 8 hours, never on one cell
Gold in the tool is an upper bound until the wage formula exists: loot is sold to the vendor at once and coin reads 1.24 times the one real four. A gold target is read as direction only until then

leverRules.rule: Balance is fixed at the formula layer. No ground, weapon or monster gets its own patch or its own math, and no parameter is added per hunting ground to hit a number. The order is content data, then a coefficient, then a curve
leverRules.source: The formula brief and the baseline directive, 2026-11-21

leverRules.rule: A blow reads only stats against stats. Never the hero's own Level, never a Level-gap multiplier or a Level penalty
A tier is a bigger pull plus percent dials on XP and difficulty. Coin per kill never scales with a tier
One difficulty for every group size: one pull, one blow and one health number a tier, one pack on Normal, and monster health never grows in a party
Party XP is paid by party size alone, one flat table for every ground and tier
No Level XP boost is sold for Crowns or gold, no odds are sold for gold, and Crowns never buy power directly
leverRules.source: Rulings 2026-10-14 and 2026-11-04. MM-29-XP, said yes on the page 2026-11-21

leverRules.rule: The sword and shield and the sword alone stay slow alone on purpose. No Level XP or damage spell is added to close their lone pace. Tank spells hold, protect and control
Nothing refuses a Level. A big risk shows a warning and one confirm press
Every supply falls back to the store. A hunt never stops for stock. Only gold that cannot pay ends it
Profit is reported, never graded. A hunt that is clearly off is looked at alone, never by a blanket mold
No healing nerf without real-engine evidence of throughput, incoming damage and resource use
Luck has two feeds only, rivets used and Bestiary stages. It is bound to the account and never sold
Events never pay over +25% and never two at once
No XP penalty for hunting under-levelled monsters. A lower ground simply pays less, and over-levelled hunting for profit is good
An approved target is never moved to make a simulation pass. A conflict is stated for Tyler

conflicts.title: The flat death count against the cliff
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: Call 5 asked for a flat count at every Level. The engine gives a cliff: a four is safe or it wipes, and the count is the thin line between. S-12 a moved the count to a four arriving in a band. Even there one table of blow and pull cannot hold every ground inside 50 to 100, and LR-1 forbids a dial per ground
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R2: of 56 Deadly ground cells, one read inside 50 to 100, forty had no death and six wiped. The replay read 44 for all Deadly cells together (run 44948522187)
conflicts.tradeoff: A single dial can aim at the pooled count over band floors. A ground that sits far off can be moved only through content data (D-10 group casters), never its own dial

conflicts.title: Dangerous's ruled floor against tier order
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: Dangerous is ruled at 10 to 30 deaths. With one blow number for both tiers it reads about 5. Reaching 10 needs Dangerous to hit harder than Deadly, which turns the tiers upside down on grounds with shooters
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED: Dangerous at 2.5 pooled 4 to 5 (R4, replay). At 3.0 it pooled 29 but was deadlier than Deadly on two grounds (R2, the Coppercap Warrens 657 against 138)
conflicts.tradeoff: S-12 a was ruled with this cost shown: "Dangerous rarely kills a mid four inside its band". The band's floor of 10 is older than that answer

conflicts.title: The old health bands against the death count
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: The Hard and Extreme rows of 2026-10-25 ask a typical low point of 35 to 60% and 15 to 40%. At the death counts of 2026-11-21 the low point reads 36 to 66%, and a four whose low point sits under 0.36 wipes
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R2: near the ruled count the median low point is 48%. Every cell under 0.36 wiped
conflicts.tradeoff: The newer ruling wins. The health rows stay as readings and the death sample judges a tier

conflicts.title: The 3 to 5% armor step against the early ladder
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: An armor upgrade is ruled at 3 to 5% less damage. The built ladder tiers 1 to 7 give about 9 to 18% each. Resampling them on the curve would leave Bronze with about 3 points of plate a set and make the Bronze to Iron step about fifteen times
conflicts.evidence: COMPUTED at armor x2.4 (D-3 section 1.3): about 18% at Level 20, 17% at 30, 13% at 45, 12% at 60 and 9% at 88. The band step past Level 110 reads 3.6 to 4.1% (MEASURED)
conflicts.tradeoff: Keep the early hook (D3-1, graded from Level 110) or meet 3 to 5% everywhere and lose the felt early upgrade

conflicts.title: Jewelry's 6% against the shipped rows
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: GR-38 sizes the crafted class at 6% of a kit at every Level. The shipped rows are typed per tier, so their share falls with Level
conflicts.evidence: Local (D-3 ruling 6): 13.9% of a lone MID hero's pace at Level 20, 11.0% at 60, 5.4% at 110, 2.2% at 400. For a four, 3.5% or less from Level 20
conflicts.tradeoff: A flat share means early rows come down and late rows go up. D-3 kept the rows for the first build because a four feels 3.5% or less and crafting should pay early

conflicts.title: Upgrade prices against band gold
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: On 2026-11-18 Tyler kept the typed prices and also ruled that standing upgrades cost more than a band earns. With four heroes from the start the typed prices fall to a fifth of a band's gold, so GEAR-9's rule fails
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R0: full best gear costs 0.18 of a band's net gold for a lone hero, against 1.2 to 1.4. All 22 rows red
conflicts.tradeoff: Keep the typed numbers and lose "choose what matters", or price upgrades as a share of band gold (GR-8) and drop the typed numbers

conflicts.title: The Level table's 100 and 400 under one seat multiple
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: One multiple can be exact at one Level only, because a seat's own reading drifts with Level. It holds both points in band while the seat's reading at 400 over its reading at 100 stays within 1.10 / 0.90, about 1.22
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R4 at 1.266: 1.005 at Level 100 and 1.115 at 400, a ratio of 1.11. The matrix lane reports 100 to 400 in band at 1.327
conflicts.tradeoff: In band is enough (2026-11-21). If a dial pushes the ratio past 1.22, the curve's shape is wrong and the fix is at the curve, never a second multiple

conflicts.title: The four together against the same four split up: the gold half
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: The ruling says more XP and gold a head. A four shares one kill stream four ways, coin per kill never scales with a tier (LR-3) and party pay is XP only (LR-5). So the four out-earns its heroes alone in gold only if its kills an hour reach four times a lone hero's
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R0: a four on Dangerous nets 0.53 to 0.77 of a lone MID hammer a head. XP a head is 1.4 to 2.6 times at 28 of 29 checkpoints
conflicts.tradeoff: Read the rule on XP only, as the 10:40 refinement and 2026-11-13 suggest, or add a gold share by party size (a new party buff), or raise the harder tiers' pull, which moves the death sample and the Level clock

conflicts.title: A fixed percent gear step against a fixed Level gap
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: GR-4 opens a band each time the linear gear curve grows 17%, so the gap is about 0.17 times the Level. It is under 25 Levels only to about Level 147 and under 30 only to about 176. A smaller step keeps the gap but the weapon step already reads under 5% at Level 185
conflicts.evidence: COMPUTED: band edges 110, 129, 151, 176, 206, 241, 282, 330 and 386. MEASURED L: the +17% step is 4.4% at Level 185
conflicts.tradeoff: Past about Level 150 keep 5 to 8% a step with wider gaps, or keep 15 to 25 Levels with smaller steps, or count reforged uniques and Tempering as the major upgrades in between

conflicts.title: Best gear's 15% against a four's respawn ceiling
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: Call 3 asks best gear to be about 15% faster. A four kills about as fast as the ground respawns, so no gear moves its pace much on Normal. The paid-edge reading of 1.65 multiplied 15% into a four's pace
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R0: best gear is 2% faster for a four on Normal and 5 to 7% on the harder tiers. Every cap full reads 1.29 to 1.48, not 1.65
conflicts.tradeoff: P4 reads a lone hero, where 15% is reachable. For a four, gear is sized as how many Levels sooner it holds the next tier (balance pass section 4.2)

conflicts.title: Full BiS in a band against the weekly chest limits
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: Call 14 puts full BiS at about a band's length to Krell. Call 6 keeps the weekly chest limits. Bands to Krell last about 3 to 11 days at 12 h, and a specific top chest piece takes weeks. The BiS kit includes chest pieces
conflicts.evidence: COMPUTED: gap 17 of 50-standards (bands of 3 to 11 days). Ruling 2026-11-16: a specific Platinum piece in about 13.5 weeks
conflicts.tradeoff: Call 6's own words, "fast players skip early chest pieces", read B1 as BiS without weekly-capped pieces to Krell. Otherwise B1 is red by construction

conflicts.title: The Dangerous clock against Deadly past the edge
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: The Level table is timed on the four on Dangerous (S-11 c), and a four moves to Deadly once it grows past the edge (S-12 a). That four runs ahead of the table
conflicts.evidence: COMPUTED (balance pass section 7, item 1): a four that farms Deadly safely runs about 18% ahead
conflicts.tradeoff: Accepted at the sitting. The runway is read on the fastest seat held all the time (GR-6a)

conflicts.title: "The rest hunt on" against the death count
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: When the front hero falls the other three die in the same hunt, so one wipe is four deaths
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED run 44948522187: 121 of 129 front-first hunts
conflicts.tradeoff: Accepted at S-14 a. The ruled counts count every hero, so 50 to 100 is one wipe in 10 to 20 party-hours

conflicts.title: R1's band against call 7
conflicts.needs: the matrix lane, if the new design keeps the candidate
conflicts.what: Call 7 says each region opens 30 days before the first fours arrive, read on the fastest seat held all the time. R1 asks 14 days, on the pace four
conflicts.evidence: standards.mjs R1: lo 14, red 0, "the four MID player"
conflicts.tradeoff: None. The band is softer than the ruling and reads another seat

conflicts.title: G-5 graded as a hard line
conflicts.needs: the matrix lane, if the new design keeps the candidate
conflicts.what: G-5 grades "an arrival four on Deadly nets at or under zero" as RULED. The 2026-11-19 ruling was given as a direction, not a hard rule, and 2026-11-13 says profit is never graded
conflicts.evidence: standards.mjs G-5: hi 0, red 0, label RULED
conflicts.tradeoff: None. It should print, not grade

conflicts.title: G-1 report only against call 24-2
conflicts.needs: the matrix lane, if the new design keeps the candidate
conflicts.what: Band change 5 made G-1 report only, citing the 2026-11-13 profit ruling. Call 24-2 came later and rules that a new ground never pays a lone hero on Normal less than the one before
conflicts.evidence: standards.mjs G-1 reportOnly. 30-decisions.json 24-2, ruled 2026-11-20

conflicts.title: P9's band against the pull
conflicts.needs: the matrix lane, if the new design keeps the candidate
conflicts.what: P9 assumes the per-kill XP alone. The 2026-11-07 ruling keeps the bigger pulls and accepts that the rate an hour rises with them
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED R0: Dangerous pays 2.1 to 3.0 times Normal for a four, so P9.dangerous is off in 646 rows
conflicts.tradeoff: None. The band does not describe the ruled mechanics

conflicts.title: P8 still standing after its twin was dropped
conflicts.needs: the matrix lane, if the new design keeps the candidate
conflicts.what: GR-67 dropped P7.4, the mid four's cap against the contract, because no party size is a target against a lone hero (2026-11-21). P8, the best-gear four's cap of 2.75 from call 30-2, is the same kind of target and still stands
conflicts.evidence: standards.mjs P8 and P7.4 (dropped)
conflicts.tradeoff: Report only, or keep it as the runway's guard and say so

conflicts.title: Krell on day 18 against the Level table
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: The 2026-11-21 morning ruling quoted day 18 for a four. The table timed on the four on Dangerous (S-11 c, later that day) puts Level 88 on about day 33
conflicts.evidence: COMPUTED in the balance pass: day 33 at seat 1.266. Reversal 2 (GR-6b) let stand on the page
conflicts.tradeoff: The operative ruling is "weeks, not months". Day 33 is about 4.7 weeks

conflicts.title: "Deadly is never the best idle tier" read literally
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: By the top of a band Deadly is safe for a mid four and pays 20 to 29% over Dangerous, so an idle four should take it there. S-12 a says so
conflicts.evidence: MEASURED run 44948522187: Deadly pays 20 to 29% over Dangerous in the upper part of each band
conflicts.tradeoff: SURV-8 holds on arrival only

conflicts.title: P11.early's red line looser than the ruling
conflicts.needs: the matrix lane, if the new design keeps the candidate
conflicts.what: Call 27-2 says no Level under 10 takes over 2 hours. P11.early reads 2 to 2.5 hours as off, not red
conflicts.evidence: standards.mjs P11.early: hi 2, red 2.5
conflicts.tradeoff: None. A breach of a ruled cap should read red

conflicts.title: The hall ship bar against D-9's reading of it
conflicts.needs: the designer decides when the new design is defined
conflicts.what: The 2026-11-05 ship bar asks about 85% on a good bar and about 30% on a bad one. D-9 makes the hall a Dangerous room, where a good bar wins about every fight from the band's middle and a bad bar about half, so it reads 85% as a floor (at least 80%) and grades the bad bar at 50% or under
conflicts.evidence: Probe C (8 fights a row): the good bar 8 of 8 at Levels 98 and 110, the bad bar 4 of 8 at 98. Probe B: the bad bar 3 and 7 of 8 at Levels 25 and 75
conflicts.tradeoff: Losing 15% to the dice on a good bar needs the clock or blows near the party's sustain, both cliffs in Level and gear. The other road is the hall at Deadly with its doubled wave, which presses the card's party harder and keeps 85% and 30% as the aim
